subject: Rollforward request: Lyra Lite integration & temporary version hold
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <sam@brighthire.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Rollforward request: Lyra Lite integration & temporary version hold

Team —

Product is planning to roll Lyra Lite (v2.0-lite) into staging for BrightHire next week. During the intake compatibility check the tokenizer mapping for a small but meaningful portion of our QA prompts failed (sentencepiece vs byte-level mismatch), which caused truncated completions in staging. I attached the compatibility matrix with the failing buckets (lyra-lite-compat-matrix.xlsx) and linked the intake ticket (JIRA INF-8421).

Ask: before we proceed to canary, I want to request a temporary version hold (pin) for the Lyra Lite variant on hosted and Dedicated lanes so we don’t start serving the current variant to production traffic until we validate the tokenization fixes and run the regression evals. Specific asks: 
- Dev: ETA on a tokenizer mapping patch and a staging deployable build?
- Rishi: any safety/regression buckets we should add to the smoke list?
- Laura & Priyom: process for a short-term pin (48–72h) and owner for canary.
- Marissa: quick cost hit estimate for keeping both variants pinned in Dedicated for 72h.

Sam (BrightHire) — FYI; we’re coordinating timing but want to avoid surfacing partial regressions to your users.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Group PM, Model Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: lyra-lite-compat-matrix.xlsx
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <sam@brighthire.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Rollforward request: Lyra Lite integration & temporary version hold

Jasmine —

Thanks for the heads-up and the compatibility matrix. I dug into the failing examples — it looks like the SentencePiece vocabulary used in the reference conversion step strips leading spaces for some tokens, while our tokenizer path expects preserved leading whitespace markers. The quick fix is a token mapping shim in the conversion layer; I can have a patch and a staging image ready by Sunday (2027-05-30) morning UTC. Deploy to staging and a small local smoke-run should follow immediately.

Notes / risks:
- The shim is non-invasive (runtime mapping), but we need to run the full KV-cache smoke to validate no cache offset drift.
- If smoke fails, rollback is cheap (switch back to lyra-lite-v1 mapping) but we should pin before any production routing.

I’ll prepare a short runbook and push a branch to the intake ticket (INF-8421) with details.

—Dev
Senior Backend Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: rollback-runbook.md
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <sam@brighthire.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 20:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Rollforward request: Lyra Lite integration & temporary version hold

Folks —

Operational perspective: we can approve a short-term pin but need three things before I sign off for canary:
1) A staging deploy with the patch and green smoke results (Dev).
2) A rollback plan + who owns the rollback (Dev + Jasmine).
3) A canary window and SLA rollback trigger thresholds documented in the runbook (Jasmine + Rishi).

If Dev can deliver the staging image on Sunday as proposed, we can schedule a limited canary next Tuesday in the 14:00–18:00 UTC window. Note: pin process requires an explicit approval recorded (DocuSign link) — I’ll route once we confirm the plan.

Marissa — can you weigh in on the cost delta for pinning both variants in Dedicated for 72 hours? A quick ballpark is fine.

Laura Bennett
Release Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <sam@brighthire.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Rollforward request: Lyra Lite integration & temporary version hold

On Fri, 28 May 2027 at 16:12 GMT Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> Product is planning to roll Lyra Lite (v2.0-lite) into staging for BrightHire next week...

Quick safety note: the initial eval sweep shows small regressions (~0.7–1.2% absolute) on the 'format-preservation' and 'command-following' buckets for lyra-lite-v2 compared with v1 baseline. Dev's tokenizer shim probably eliminates the truncation failure, but we should run the expanded regression harness (10k prompts across the flagged buckets) after the staging deploy and before canary.

Recommendation: require the 10k-run to pass a soft-threshold (no more than 0.8% regression on any single bucket) and hold the pin for 72 hours after canary to observe real traffic signals. If regression shows up in canary, auto-fallback to lyra-lite-v1 should be configured.

I’ll add the new test set to INF-8421 and can run the post-deploy sweep within 4 hours of the staging image being available.

—Rishi
Research Engineer, Model Quality & Safety
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <sam@brighthire.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 16:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Rollforward request: Lyra Lite integration & temporary version hold

Jasmine / Laura —

Finance view: short pin (48–72h) has minimal incremental cost for Hosted, and Dedicated cost depends on whether we keep reserved instances warm or spin up burst capacity. Ballpark: $2.5k–$8k incremental for a 72-hour pin in Dedicated depending on pool sizing (I’ll need the exact instance counts to firm up).

Approval: fine from finance for a 72-hour temporary pin provided a follow-up ticket is created to reconcile any overage against the BrightHire commit (or issue a credit if we under-deliver). Please send me the final DocuSign approval.

—Marissa Cole
Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Thanks everyone — plan below and I’ll open the DocuSign approval: 

Plan summary: 
- Dev: push tokenizer shim to staging by 2027-05-30 08:00 UTC and attach smoke logs to INF-8421.
- Rishi: run post-deploy regression sweep (10k prompts) within 4 hours of staging deploy; soft-threshold 0.8%.
- Laura: schedule canary Tue 2027-06-01 14:00–18:00 UTC and submit pin approval once staging is green.
- Marissa: finance approved ballpark; will reconcile after pin.
- Pin duration: request 72 hours post-canary; fallback to lyra-lite-v1 if any threshold breach.

Attachments: rollback-runbook.md, canary-schedule.ics
Drive plan: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/lyra-lite-rollforward-plan
DocuSign: https://docusign.net/lyra-lite-pin-approval

I’ll file the formal pin request once we have green smoke. Sam / Alex — we’ll coordinate final timing and keep you updated.

—Jasmine
